name: Autosomal Dominant Brachyolmia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Autosomal Dominant Brachyolmia

criteria.description: Presence of disproportionate short stature with short trunk
Radiological evidence of platyspondyly (flattened vertebral bodies)
Radiographic abnormalities of the pelvis including short iliac wings and irregular acetabular roofs
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variants in the CANT1 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of disproportionate short trunk dwarfism with characteristic radiological findings (platyspondyly and pelvic abnormalities) plus either positive family history or pathogenic CANT1 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and radiological features are definitive.

imaging: Pelvic X-rays with short iliac wings and irregular acetabular roofs
Spinal MRI to assess for cord compression if neurological symptoms present
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Earlier onset and more pronounced platyspondyly

redFlags: Rapid progression of neurological symptoms indicating spinal cord compression
Severe respiratory distress due to thoracic cage deformity
Marked worsening of scoliosis or kyphosis causing functional impairment
references: Superti-Furga A, Unger S. Brachyolmia. In: GeneReviews® [Internet]. University of Washington, Seattle; 2020.
